body:
The Sun Warms Things: 1. It makes the sand warm. 2. A tree blocking the sunlight (anything that blocks the sun). 3. In the shade. 4. Answers vary; a good answer gives a reason, such as "in the shade, because it is cooler".
Sun or Shade: Which Is Warmer?: 1. Warm (or hot). 2. Cool (or cooler). 3. The one in the sun. 4. Because the sun shone on it, or because sunlight warms things. 5. Drawing shows one object in the sun and one in the shade. On a cloudy day results may be close; accept "about the same" and repeat the test on a sunny day.
Make Some Shade: the drawing shows something that sits between the sun and the sandbox, such as a roof, an umbrella, a tent, a tree or a sheet on poles, and the student tells that it blocks the sunlight.
Sun and Shade Check: 1. The slide. 2. It is in the shade of the tree; the tree blocks the sunlight. 3. Sunlight (the sun). 4. Cooler. 5. Drawing shows something blocking the sun, such as a tree, umbrella or roof.
Scoring tip: "the slide is metal" alone is Getting there on "I can tell that sunlight warms things"; look for the sun as the reason. For the design, any idea that blocks sunlight is Got it! even if it would be hard to build.
title: Answer key: Sun and Shade
